reasons: **Safety comes first, but it's close.** This plan keeps the crew's body heat just under the safe limit. Even the hottest-running workers stay less than a tenth of a degree below it, so watch for warning signs and stick to the planned breaks.
**Emma is protected.** She's new and her body isn't used to working in this heat yet, so she won't be given the hardest physical jobs during the hottest parts of the day.

**We get a bit less done to stay safer.** This plan finishes about 81% of the most important work. Two other options would finish about 84%, including one that moves the trenching into the cool morning. But both push the crew's body heat slightly closer to the limit, so we chose the safer plan.

calls.prompt:
Write 3 short plain-language bullet points (no jargon) for a crew lead explaining this schedule's trade-offs. Facts:
Peak 90th pct core temp 37.92 °C (limit 38.0), tightest margin 0.07 °C, 81% of priority-weighted work done.
Emma (new hire) is not acclimatized: no very heavy work in high heat.
Alternatives: llm-idea:Front-load trenching into the cool morning (84% work, peak 37.95 °C); optimizer:throughput (84% work, peak 37.93 °C)
calls.response:
- **Safety comes first, but it's close.** This plan keeps the crew's body heat just under the safe limit. Even the hottest-running workers stay less than a tenth of a degree below it, so watch for warning signs and stick to the planned breaks.

- **Emma is protected.** She's new and her body isn't used to working in this heat yet, so she won't be given the hardest physical jobs during the hottest parts of the day.

- **We get a bit less done to stay safer.** This plan finishes about 81% of the most important work. Two other options would finish about 84%, including one that moves the trenching into the cool morning. But both push the crew's body heat slightly closer to the limit, so we chose the safer plan.
